chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no pre-emption in a ship, nor in a river, nor in a road.'

key_terms.سَفِينَة: Ship; a vessel used for navigation, considered a common property here.
key_terms.شُفْعَة: Pre-emption; the right of a co-owner or neighbor to buy a share before it is sold to an outsider.
key_terms.طَرِيق: Road; a public way, considered a common property.
key_terms.نَهَر: River; a flowing body of water, considered a common property.

ai.seo_question: What properties are exempt from the right of pre-emption (shuf'ah) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the scope of 'shuf'ah' (pre-emption) by excluding public domains like ships, rivers, and roads, thereby preventing individual monopolization of communal resources. This ruling aligns with the principle of 'ibadah' (common use) for such assets, a distinction emphasized by scholars like Al-Shaykh al-Mufid to ensure equitable access for all Muslims.
